The image shows very young soybean seedlings that have collapsed/wilted severely near the soil line in sandy soil. The stems are green but plants are falling over with yellowed/brown dying leaves. This pattern strongly suggests a seedling damping-off disease.

Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off**, **Rhizoctonia**, **Phytophthora**, **Fusarium**

Let me view reference images for these candidates.
The Phytophthora reference closely matches the collapsed dead seedlings. Let me also check Anthracnose since it can cause seedling collapse.

Anthracnose clearly doesn't match (mature plant/pod disease). 

**Initial prediction: Pythium_damping_off** - very young seedlings completely collapsed at soil level in sandy soil, consistent with post-emergence damping-off.

Now reading the Attractor Guide.

Pythium_damping_off is not listed as an over-predicted class, so no alternative review needed. My prediction stands.

The test image shows very young soybean seedlings (cotyledon to early trifoliate stage) that have completely collapsed near the soil line in sandy soil. The plants are wilted/fallen over with dying leaves — classic post-emergence damping-off pattern. This matches Pythium_damping_off best: rotted roots causing complete seedling collapse, water-soaked soft rot at hypocotyl.

Rhizoctonia would show reddish-brown dry firm cankers (not visible here). Phytophthora would show chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward from soil. Neither is clearly evident.
